The `codec` module: deterministic CBOR profile (RFC 8949 s4.2) encoder/decoder — duplicate map keys, non-canonical integer/length encodings, and wrong major types reject fail-closed; unknown fields accepted, preserved byte-stable, re-emitted canonically on rewrite. The core KAT manifest job (merge-blocking, native + WASM), created in this slice: manifest completeness, codec accept/reject vectors, proptest encode-decode identity incl. unknown-field byte-stable round-trip; failing seeds committed as regression vectors.

1	# crates/core — v2 blueprint
2	
3	Resolved by [Blueprint: core](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/43).
4	Normative for the v2 build. Upstream inputs: the
5	[schema/envelope](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/27),
6	[sync/refresh](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/33),
7	[rotation completeness](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/38), and
8	[seal authentication](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/39) designs,
9	scoped by the [component decomposition](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/28)
10	(D2/D3). The schema amendment pile those tickets accumulated is folded in here as
11	base structure — nothing below is an "amendment" anymore.
12	
13	## Doctrine
14	
15	`crates/core` is the **pure, deterministic** layer: wire formats, the crypto
16	suite, seal/unseal, the KDF edge catalog, and IPNS record create/sign/verify —
17	one Rust implementation, linked natively by desktop and compiled to WASM for the
18	web. It performs no I/O, holds no state, reads no clock, and generates no
19	randomness of its own: entropy, timestamps, and TTL/EOL policy values enter as
20	explicit parameters (KATs pin them). Everything stateful — floors, caches, the
21	adoption-gate _pipeline_, transports — lives one crate up in `engine`; core
22	exports the pure checks the gate composes.
23	
24	What dies relative to v1 — with the design that killed it:
25	
26	| Gone                                                                      | Killed by                                                |
27	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
28	| TS/Rust twin implementations, lockstep KATs, the 8-row divergence table   | #27 D2 — one Rust core, TS keeps no codec or crypto      |
29	| JSON fixed-field-order determinism, base64 fields, decimal-string bigints | #27 D1 — deterministic CBOR everywhere                   |
30	| AES-256-GCM/CTR suite, 45-byte AAD, role bytes                            | #27 D3/D4 — XChaCha20-Poly1305, structured AAD           |
31	| eciesjs-default ECIES envelope (library-defined layout)                   | #27 D3 — RFC 9180 HPKE, spec-defined, full-envelope KATs |
32	| Per-node `ipnsPrivateKey` storage + `reconstruct_write_body` recovery     | #26/#27 D6 — write plane fully derived                   |
33	| `readKeySealed` child wraps, kind-blind child refs                        | #27 D7 — derivation + immutable `kind` in the ref        |
34	| VaultKeyBlob v3, vault-init/export endpoints                              | #27 D9 — derived vault pointer + owner blob              |
35	| `deny_unknown_fields` vs tolerant-decode contradiction                    | #27 D10 — tolerate + round-trip, one policy              |
36	| Three validity parsers at two strictness levels across five packages      | #28 D2/D3 — one strict codec, exported from core         |
37	| Content self-seal role `0x03` (built, vector-locked, dormant)             | not carried — no v2 analog                               |
38	
39	## Module map
40	
41	Functional decomposition, not final file layout:
42	
43	- **codec** — the deterministic CBOR profile; envelope, body, and structure
44	  codecs; unknown-field round-trip.
45	- **suite** — primitive bindings: XChaCha20-Poly1305, BLAKE3, X25519/HPKE,
46	  secp256k1 ECDSA, Ed25519. Pure RustCrypto; constant-time; key material in
47	  `Zeroizing` owning types (type-enforced, never comment-enforced).
48	- **kdf** — the frozen edge catalog (below); nothing derives a key outside it.
49	- **seal** — AAD construction, seal/unseal, structure signatures, the pure
50	  verify functions the adoption gate composes.
51	- **ipns** — record create/sign/marshal/unmarshal/verify, name codec.
52	- **kat** — the vector manifest and fixtures (regime below).
53	
54	## Wire format
55	
56	- **DAG-CBOR** for every published block (envelope, pointer payload); the same
57	  deterministic profile (RFC 8949 §4.2) for sealed-body plaintext and every
58	  signed structure. Native byte strings and u64s; determinism is a property of
59	  the encoder, not a field-order convention.
60	- **One strictness policy, everywhere.** Decoders accept deterministic-profile
61	  CBOR only: duplicate map keys, non-canonical integer/length encodings, and
62	  wrong major types reject fail-closed. The single tolerance is **unknown
63	  fields**: accepted, ignored for logic, preserved byte-stable, and re-emitted
64	  canonically on rewrite — an old client rewriting under shared write never
65	  strips newer fields (#27 D10).
66	- **Uniqueness fail-closed** (#39 D7): duplicate `id`s anywhere, and duplicate
67	  `ipnsName`s within a scope, reject at decode.
68	- **Versioning**: a single small-int `v` on the envelope covers format + crypto
69	  suite, bound into the AAD so downgrade fails the tag. Additive changes never
70	  bump it; any breaking change bumps and forces re-seal — expensive by design.
71	  No body-level schema strings (#27 D5).
72	
73	## Crypto suite
74	
75	| Role                       | Algorithm                                               | Used for                                                                        |
76	| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
77	| Symmetric sealing          | XChaCha20-Poly1305 (24-byte nonce)                      | All sealed bodies and structures, content bytes                                 |
78	| Key derivation             | BLAKE3 `derive_key` / `keyed_hash`                      | The whole edge catalog                                                          |
79	| Sealing to a person        | RFC 9180 HPKE (X25519-HKDF-SHA256 + XChaCha20-Poly1305) | Grant blobs, owner blob, ascent links, mailbox payloads                         |
80	| Pairwise secrets           | X25519 ECDH                                             | Blinded tags, pseudonym derivation                                              |
81	| Identity signing           | secp256k1 ECDSA (RFC 6979) over det-CBOR                | Grant-set commitment, subkey binding, re-point object, mailbox sender signature |
82	| Pseudonym + record signing | Ed25519                                                 | Structure signatures; IPNS records                                              |
83	
84	- Every user derives an **X25519 encryption subkey** from their login secret;
85	  the identity key only signs, the subkey only seals. The **subkey binding**
86	  (ECDSA over det-CBOR `{identityPk, encSubkey}`) and the **contact code**
87	  codec (`{identityPk, encSubkey, bindingSig}`, ~130 bytes, QR/URL-encodable,
88	  binding verify mandatory and fail-closed at import) are core exports.
89	- Writer pseudonyms sign with **Ed25519** (deterministic derivation from the
90	  pairwise secret; secp256k1 stays confined to identity signing per #27 D3).
91	- HPKE envelopes are spec-defined with a full-envelope KAT under a fixed
92	  ephemeral key — the eciesjs lesson (a library major bump must never be able
93	  to silently orphan stored ciphertexts).
94	
95	## Envelope and structures
96	
97	Kind-uniform envelope (#27 D4): `{v, id, epochTag{scope, epoch}, readSealed,
98	writeSealed?, grantSection?}` — `kind` lives inside the sealed read-body, so
99	observers cannot distinguish files from folders. Scope id = the scope root's
100	node UUID.
101	
102	- **AAD** = `(v, id, scope, epoch, structTag)` under a fresh `cipherbox/v2`
103	  domain separator. `ipnsName` is deliberately **not** in the AAD (#39 D7 —
104	  the name wave republishes epoch-lagged bodies under fresh names; transplant
105	  is closed by duplicate rejection instead).
106	- **Read-body**: tagged union `folder {children[]}` | `file {versions[]}` plus
107	  `createdAt`/`modifiedAt` (injected timestamps). Versions are one inline
108	  newest-first list `[{contentCid, contentKey, size, modifiedAt}]`, head =
109	  current. Content keys are random per version — never derived, rotation
110	  re-wraps them via the metadata re-seal.
111	- **Child refs**: `{id, name, ipnsName, kind, linkCounter}` — immutable fields
112	  plus the monotonic link counter that picks the deterministic loser in
113	  dual-link repair (#33 D5). No key wraps, no size/mtime mirrors: child writes
114	  never republish the parent.
115	- **Write-body** (scope roots only, #27 D6): `{grant ledger, write-plane
116	history link, directChildScopeIndex}` sealed under the root's writeKey. The
117	  ledger is `(recipientIdentityPk, recipientEncPk, permission, tag)`; the
118	  child-scope index enumerates directly-descendant scope roots for the F-4
119	  rotation cascade (#38 D6). Interior nodes publish no write-body at all.
120	- **Grant section** (scope roots only): grant blobs keyed by blinded tag
121	  (`tag → HPKE{readScopeSeed[, writeScopeSeed], epoch, pointerReadKey}`), the
122	  epoch-free grant-set commitment (ECDSA over det-CBOR `{ipnsName,
123	ownerPseudonymPk, [(tag, permission, pseudonymPk)]}`), owner blob, ascent
124	  link (public half plaintext, derive-and-verified by ancestor readers),
125	  per-epoch history links, and a detached **structure signature** per
126	  seed-bearing structure.
127	- **Structure signatures** (#39 D2/D3): the rotator's pseudonym Ed25519
128	  signature over det-CBOR `{scopeId, epoch, structTag, recipientTag?,
129	H(ciphertext)}` — covering grant blobs, owner blob, ascent link, history
130	  links, and the write-body. Verification is per-structure and pure; the
131	  whole-record fail-closed policy is the engine's gate stage.
132	- **Pointer payloads**: the re-point object `{scopeId, currentRootName,
133	writeEpoch, minReadEpoch, prevRootName}`, owner-identity-signed inside the
134	  record, sealed under the scope's stable `pointerReadKey`. The vault pointer
135	  carries the same object for the root scope (#39 D5). Mailbox payloads are
136	  HPKE-sealed with a sender identity signature inside the seal (#39 D9); core
137	  owns their codecs and verify functions.
138	
139	### Structure-tag registry
140	
141	The `structTag` byte-space is the domain-separation registry, frozen in the KAT
142	manifest: `read-body`, `write-body`, `grant-blob`, `owner-blob`, `ascent-link`,
143	`history-link`, `pointer-payload`, `mailbox-payload`. Every new tag extends the
144	manifest and its vectors before merge.
145	
146	## KDF edge catalog
147	
148	Frozen per #39 D8 (F-9). Per-node material takes the shape
149	`keyed_hash(key = derive_key("<edge context>", seed), message = id16)` — ids
150	are fixed-length message input, **never** variable context. Context strings
151	follow `cipherbox/v2/<edge>`; the exact string table and input layouts freeze
152	in the KAT manifest.
153	
154	| Edge                | Inputs                                                   | Output                             |
155	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
156	| node-seed           | scopeSeed, node id                                       | nodeSeed (flat within scope)       |
157	| read-key            | nodeSeed                                                 | readKey                            |
158	| structure-key       | nodeSeed or scope seed, structTag                        | per-structure sealing keys         |
159	| write-seed          | writeScopeSeed, node id                                  | writeSeed (flat)                   |
160	| write-key           | writeSeed                                                | writeKey                           |
161	| ipns-keypair        | writeSeed                                                | Ed25519 keypair → ipnsName         |
162	| ascent-keypair      | parent nodeSeed                                          | X25519 keypair for the ascent link |
163	| enc-subkey          | login secret                                             | X25519 encryption subkey           |
164	| blinded-tag         | ECDH(ownerEnc, recipientEnc) ‖ scopeRootIpnsName         | grant-blob tag                     |
165	| pseudonym-sign      | ECDH(ownerEnc, writerEnc) ‖ scopeId (owner: root secret) | Ed25519 pseudonym keypair          |
166	| owner-pointer-seed  | login secret                                             | ownerPointerSeed                   |
167	| scope-pointer       | ownerPointerSeed, scope id                               | per-scope pointer Ed25519 keypair  |
168	| pointer-read-key    | ownerPointerSeed, scope id                               | pointerReadKey                     |
169	| vault-pointer-index | login secret, index i (0 default)                        | pointer Ed25519 keypair chain      |
170	
171	Non-edges, stated to stay non-edges: content keys (random per version), scope
172	override seeds (random at rotation), scope seeds at grant cuts (random).
173	
174	## IPNS records
175	
176	Core owns records end-to-end on both platforms (#28 D2); transports are dumb
177	byte movers injected by the engine.
178	
179	- **Create/sign**: spec-compliant V2 records (`signatureV2` over the CBOR data
180	  field; V1 fields emitted for ecosystem compatibility), `Value =
181	/ipfs/<CID>` of the DAG-CBOR envelope. First publish embeds sequence 1; CAS
182	  publishes embed the exact expected sequence. Validity = 90-day client-signed
183	  EOL (#24); TTL always explicitly set, value injected from the sync timing
184	  profile (#33 D3) — core never defaults it.
185	- **Verify**: the full chain, pure — Ed25519 pubkey extracted from the name
186	  itself (identity multihash; never a side channel or DB column), `signatureV2`
187	  verify, data-field/Value consistency, EOL and sequence extraction for the
188	  gate's comparators. Verdict-vector KATs pin the acceptance domain.
189	- **Name codec**: `ipnsName` = base36 CIDv1 libp2p-key of the Ed25519 public
190	  key. Encode + strict decode are core exports; everything downstream treats
191	  names as opaque.
192	- **Keyless re-PUT** is a first-class shape: marshal/unmarshal round-trips a
193	  foreign signed record byte-stable without key material (the republisher and
194	  every accelerator depend on this).
195	
196	## KAT regime
197	
198	Single-implementation scope (#27 D2): KATs no longer defend cross-language
199	parity — they defend the **frozen contract** against future drift (refactors,
200	dependency majors, WASM-target divergence) and pin the acceptance domain.
201	
202	- **One machine-checked manifest** enumerates every frozen encoding — envelope
203	  and structure codecs, AAD layout, the KDF edge catalog with exact context
204	  strings, HPKE envelope, structure-signature preimages, IPNS record and name
205	  codecs, the structure-tag registry — and the vector files that lock each.
206	  Tests and CI consume the manifest; "what is KAT-locked" is never folklore
207	  (the v1 lesson).
208	- **Accept and reject vectors for every codec**: malformed-input verdicts are
209	  part of the frozen contract from day one — duplicate keys, non-canonical
210	  encodings, wrong types, truncations, AAD transplants, bad signatures.
211	- **Separation KAT**: no two catalog edges may produce equal output for equal
212	  inputs — asserted mechanically over the whole edge table.
213	- **Fixed-parameter full-envelope KATs**: symmetric seals under fixed key +
214	  nonce; HPKE under a fixed ephemeral key; IPNS records under fixed keys and
215	  injected timestamps. Purity makes every path KAT-able.
216	- **Anti-vacuity**: vector counts and tag/edge coverage are hard-asserted and
217	  bumped with the fixture; vectors with real crypto material come from
218	  committed generators, never hand-edits.
219	- **WASM is the residual parity surface**: the same suite runs natively and as
220	  WASM in CI — one implementation, two compilation targets; boundary risks
221	  (u64/BigInt, getrandom wiring) are covered by running the KATs there, not by
222	  a second vector set.
223	
224	## Error surface
225	
226	Two classes, disjoint types, no reused codes (v1 defect): **trust violations**
227	(signature, commitment, structure-signature, AAD, uniqueness, canonicality
228	failures — the engine treats these fail-closed) and **malformed/availability**
229	errors. Unseal failure never silently degrades; every rejection names the
230	check that fired.
231	
232	## Open edges
233	
234	- Content chunking format and version-retention policy — client policy, owned
235	  by the [engine blueprint](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/44);
236	  core ships the content-seal primitive over caller-framed chunks.
237	- Exact context-string table, structure-tag bytes, and vector fixtures freeze
238	  in the KAT manifest at build time; CI wiring for the manifest check belongs
239	  to the [testing strategy](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/47).
240	- WASM packaging, worker hosting, and the JS type boundary —
241	  [web client blueprint](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/45)
242	  over `crates/wasm` + `packages/client`.

1	# CipherBox v2 — Ubiquitous Language
2	
3	Glossary only. Design detail lives in `blueprint/`; the as-built v1 spec corpus, ADRs, and decision history live in [FSM1/cipher-box-next](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next).
4	
5	## Read-plane key model (seeded derivation)
6	
7	- **Node seed** — the per-node secret from which a node's keys derive, flat within a scope: `nodeSeed(X) = KDF(scopeSeed, X.id)`. Location-independent, so intra-scope moves are pure relinks; membership is the envelope's epoch tag.
8	- **Scope** — a derivation domain: the set of nodes keyed from one random scope seed. The vault root is the initial scope; every grant on an interior folder and every rotation creates or re-seeds one.
9	- **Scope root** — the node a scope is anchored at, carrying its grant blobs, owner blob, ascent link, and history links. Granting an interior folder makes it a scope root (with a subtree sweep into the new scope).
10	- **Content key** — a random per-version key stored inline in the sealed read-body. Rotation re-wraps it for free via the metadata re-seal and never re-encrypts content bytes; the next version is fresh-keyed. There is no pending-re-key state.
11	- **Cross-scope move** — moving a node between scopes re-seals the moved subtree at the destination scope's epoch (and is a scope exit for the source when the source is granted).
12	- **Override seed** — the fresh random seed minted at a scope root by a rotation, replacing its derived (or prior override) seed and starting a new epoch.
13	- **Epoch** — a scope-relative rotation counter. Every sealed body carries a plaintext, AAD-bound **epoch tag** `{scope, epoch}`.
14	- **Ascent link** — the current override seed sealed to an asymmetric keypair derived from the _parent's_ node seed (never the child's own): the public half rides plaintext in the scope root's envelope so any writer can re-seal the link; unsealing requires the parent seed, so only ancestor-scope readers descend. Ancestor readers re-derive the expected keypair and reject a mismatched public half. Deliberately unreadable to holders of the scope's own prior seed.
15	- **Owner blob** — the current override seed ECIES-wrapped to the vault owner's identity key, present at every scope root and maintained by whoever rotates. The owner is an implicit, permanent, unrevokable grantee of every scope. An accelerator for owner entry — the canonical path is the owner seed cache; cross-checked against the ascent link and actual unseals, with disagreement raised as attributable abuse.
16	- **Owner seed cache** — the owner's self-authored `{seed, epoch}` per granted scope, kept in the owner's own vault share list and refreshed on every confirmed owner read. The canonical owner entry into any scope; a rogue rotator can withhold at most the epochs minted since the owner's last visit.
17	- **History link** — the previous epoch's seed sealed under the current one; the key-regression ratchet. Current-seed holders walk backward to read not-yet-resealed nodes; old-seed holders can never walk forward.
18	- **Lazy wave** — post-rotation re-sealing of a scope's descendants at the new epoch, carried by ordinary writes and/or a background sweep rather than an eager cascade.
19	- **Epoch lag** — a node whose envelope epoch is behind its scope's current epoch; readable via history links, queued for the lazy wave. Replaces v1's "dirty edge".
20	- **Eager set** — the nodes a revocation rotation must republish before it counts as cut: the rotated scope root plus every transitively-reachable descendant scope root, each fully rotated — the live-grant qualifier is retired, since a revokee may hold cached descendant seeds (grant-less scopes are cheap: an empty blob set). A grantee scope-exit rotation revokes nobody and stays flat. Interior nodes ride the lazy wave.
21	- **Epoch-converged** — a subtree with no epoch-lagged nodes. Granting a subtree requires converging it first (a new grantee cannot regress through an ancestor scope's history).
22	
23	## Write-plane key model
24	
25	- **Write seed** — the write plane's parallel derivation, flat within a write scope: `writeSeed(X) = KDF(writeScopeSeed, X.id)`. A node's Ed25519 IPNS keypair, its `ipnsName`, and its `writeKey` all derive from its write seed. Read grants carry read seeds only; write grants carry both.
26	- **Write-scope cut** — granting write on an interior folder anchors a fresh write scope there: flat derivation means one node's write seed cannot derive its children's, so the grant mints a write scope seed and runs a name wave over the subtree.
27	- **Name wave** — the background, child-first republish of a write-rotated scope under freshly derived names, root re-pointed last. Survivor write-grantees derive new names locally; read-only survivors follow republished mirrors (root re-point via the scope pointer; mailbox and old-name tombstone as accelerators).
28	- **Forgery window** — accepted residual: during the name wave a revoked writer can still seal plausible old-epoch records at not-yet-rotated old names. Wave-bounded for write-grantee survivors (they derive every new name locally); for read-only survivors, at most ~one pointer-consult interval past the re-point publish (a sync-timing-profile constant). Old names retire from the republisher inventory (tombstones advisory only).
29	
30	## Envelope and grants
31	
32	- **Envelope** — the published plaintext wrapper of a node: format version, node id, epoch tag, the sealed bodies, and (at scope roots only) the grant section. Kind-uniform: whether a node is a file or a folder is sealed inside the read-body.
33	- **Write-body** — the sealed write-plane payload, present only at scope roots: the grant ledger plus the write-plane history link. Interior nodes publish none; all their write material is derived.
34	- **Blinded tag** — the opaque per-pair label a grant blob is keyed by, derived from an owner–recipient shared secret and the scope root's name. Observers learn only blob count; the recipient self-locates their blob.
35	- **Grant blob** — a scope's current seed(s) sealed to one recipient and keyed by their blinded tag, carried in the scope root's envelope. Read grants carry the read seed; write grants carry both seeds.
36	- **Grant ledger** — the authoritative record of a scope's grants, `(recipient, permission, tag)`, sealed in the scope root's write-body. Writers re-wrap blobs for the recorded set during re-seals but cannot change the set; grant changes are owner-only.
37	- **Grant-set commitment** — the owner-signed `(tag, permission, pseudonymPk)` list in the scope root's envelope, plus the owner's own pseudonym key. Recipients verify their tag is committed before trusting a grant. Binds tag membership and writer pseudonyms only — never blob contents. Deliberately epoch-free, so grantee-triggered rotation needs no owner signature.
38	- **Writer pseudonym** — the per-(scope, writer) signing keypair derived from the same pairwise ECDH secret as the blinded tag; its public key rides the grant-set commitment. Any envelope holder verifies committed-write authorship; only ledger readers map a pseudonym to an identity; observers see nothing linkable across scopes.
39	- **Structure signature** — the rotator's detached pseudonym signature over a seed-bearing structure's ciphertext and context `{scope, epoch, structure tag, recipient tag}`, carried by grant blobs, the owner blob, ascent and history links, and the write-body. A missing or invalid signature is a whole-record trust violation at the adoption gate.
40	- **Encryption subkey** — the sealing key each user derives from their login secret, published signed by their identity key. The identity key only signs; the subkey only seals.
41	- **Scope pointer** — the owner-keyed stable IPNS name every shared scope carries, `pointerKey(scope) = KDF(ownerPointerSeed, scope.id)`. Its record holds the re-point object; consulted on the sync tick for open shared scopes, on access for cached ones, and first on cold start.
42	- **Re-point object** — the owner-identity-signed `{scopeId, currentRootName, writeEpoch, minReadEpoch, prevRootName}` payload, published at the scope pointer (canonical) and mirrored to the mailbox and the old name's tombstone as accelerators. The cold-start floor anchor: `minReadEpoch` is bumped only by owner-triggered read rotations, so grantee rotations need no owner signature yet revocation boundaries cannot be rolled back.
43	- **Floor law** — floors advance only on an AAD-confirmed unseal and cold-seed from the re-point object's owner-vouched epochs, never from a raw blob field; a grant blob's epoch field is an advisory routing hint.
44	- **Vault pointer** — the indexed IPNS name chain derived from the owner's login secret, `pointerKey_i = KDF(secret, "vault-pointer" ‖ i)`, index 0 default; its record carries the root scope's re-point object. The cold-boot entry point; root write rotation re-points it. Clients probe one index past the highest known and adopt the highest valid owner-signed payload; an owner-side index bump is the pointer-key-compromise recovery.
45	
46	## Sync and refresh
47	
48	- **Sync timing profile** — the environment-scoped bundle of sync timing policy: record TTL, poll cadence, staleness thresholds, offline staging budget, escalation window. Records always set TTL explicitly; TTL is independent of EOL.
49	- **Focus window** — the set a poll tick refreshes: the vault pointer, the open folder, and its ancestor chain to root. Everything else refreshes on access.
50	- **Pending-op overlay** — the client state law: rendered state is the last-known-good remote snapshot with queued ops applied on top; the op queue is the only local divergence.
51	- **Op queue** — the durable FIFO journal of intent ops every mutation rides. Offline replay and online CAS rebase re-apply ops through the same path.
52	- **Adoption gate** — the trust pipeline every resolved record passes before adoption: signature verify, commitment verify, structure signatures against committed write pseudonyms (scope roots), strictly-newer sequence vs floor, epoch at or above the scope floor, unseal success. A failure is a fail-closed trust violation, never mere staleness.
53	- **Conditional delete** — a delete op snapshots its target's own record sequence; on rebase it is dropped if the target advanced. Edit wins in both directions: a rebased edit resurrects a concurrently deleted node.
54	- **Observed repair** — cleanup of an invariant violation noticed at read time by any write-capable client, e.g. removing the losing link of a dual-linked child.
55	- **Dual-link** — one child linked in two parents, the benign crash residue of a dest-first move; repaired deterministically via the child ref's monotonic link counter.
56	- **Dead-letter** — a queued op that terminally fails rebase, surfaced to the user with any staged content preserved rather than silently dropped.
57	- **Withheld-update escalation** — the shared-scope warning raised when a name stays pinned past a profile window while other resolves succeed; the reader-side signal for a stale-view pin.
58	
59	## Core crate
60	
61	- **KDF edge catalog** — the frozen enumeration of every key-derivation edge (context string + input layout) in `crates/core`; nothing derives a key outside it. Per-node material is `keyed_hash(key = derive_key("<edge context>", seed), message = id16)` — ids are fixed-length message input, never variable context.
62	- **Structure tag** — the domain-separation registry entry naming each sealed/signed structure (read-body, write-body, grant-blob, owner-blob, ascent-link, history-link, pointer-payload, mailbox-payload); bound into the AAD and the structure-signature preimage.
63	- **KAT manifest** — the machine-checked enumeration of every frozen encoding and the vector files locking each; tests and CI consume it, so the KAT'd surface is auditable rather than folklore.
64	- **Acceptance domain** — the part of the frozen contract covering what a codec rejects: reject-vectors (duplicate keys, non-canonical encodings, transplants, bad signatures) ship alongside accept-vectors from day one.
65	- **Separation KAT** — the mechanical assertion that no two KDF edges produce equal output for equal inputs, run over the whole edge table.
66	
67	## API residual surface
68	
69	- **Name inventory** — the per-account `(account, ipnsName)` registry feeding the republisher. Membership derives from pin registration on the publish path, never from a side-channel.
70	- **Register-first** — the fail-closed ordering law: a name/CID batch registers before its first publish, and publish blocks on it. Live-but-uninventoried is structurally impossible; the residual failure is a registered-never-published orphan, alert-GC'd.
71	- **Union liveness** — a name stays in the republish inventory while any account holds a row for it; it leaves when the last row retires. Physical unpin fires at global refcount zero.
72	- **Advisory pin row** — a BYO account's registration: counted for union liveness and the inventory, never quota-enforced; the bytes live on the user's own provider.
73	- **Root linger** — after a write rotation, the old scope-root name stays registered serving the owner-signed `movedTo` record until the migration window closes; interior old names retire at wave completion.
74	- **Read accelerator** — CipherBox's token-authed Kubo trustless gateway. A member convenience on the read path; any public trustless gateway is the no-auth fallback.
75	- **Recovery endpoint** — authenticated fetch of non-canonical cached record bytes by name; the revival aid after a >EOL liveness lapse, on no client resolve path.
76	- **Contact code** — the self-authenticating bundle `{identityPk, encSubkey, bindingSig}` exchanged out-of-band (QR/URL); binding verification at import is mandatory and fail-closed. Replaces any people directory.
77	- **Mailbox** — the API's integrity-untrusted sealed-pointer transport: post to a recipient pubkey, poll, ack-deletes; bounded until-acked retention. Every payload is sender-identity-signed inside the seal, verified against the contact-code-anchored key; unauthenticated items are dropped. Carries discovery and courtesy traffic only, nothing load-bearing for safety.
78

1	# Testing and verification strategy — v2 blueprint
2	
3	Resolved by [Blueprint: testing and verification strategy](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/47).
4	Normative for the v2 build. Upstream inputs: the
5	[component decomposition](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/28)
6	(D6/D7), the
7	[sync/refresh/offline](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/33)
8	design (the timing profile), the KAT regime in
9	[`blueprint/core.md`](core.md), the seam contracts and facade law in
10	[`blueprint/engine.md`](engine.md), the testing hooks in
11	[`blueprint/web-client.md`](web-client.md) and
12	[`blueprint/desktop.md`](desktop.md), and the contract-and-clients section of
13	[`blueprint/api.md`](api.md). This doc fixes the suite map, the CI gates, and
14	the disposition of every v1 harness; per #28 D7, v2 rebuilds in the cipher-box
15	repo, so "ports" below means edited in place, in history.
16	
17	## Doctrine
18	
19	Verification follows the architecture. v2 concentrates all logic in two Rust
20	crates below a facade, so the test budget concentrates the same way:
21	correctness is proven **once**, in Rust, at the layer that owns it; hosts test
22	only hosting; e2e tests only flows. Three laws, each a v1 inversion:
23	
24	1. **A suite that does not block a merge does not exist.** v1's evidence:
25	   `apps/web` had a vitest config and no CI runner; `.spec.ts` files sat
26	   silently outside a `.test.ts` include; web and desktop e2e ran only
27	   post-merge, discovering regressions after they landed; an entire auth
28	   Playwright scaffold (`tests/e2e/`) was never even committed. Every v2 suite
29	   is wired into a named gate in this doc the day it lands, or it is deleted.
30	2. **Assert behavior, never source text.** v1 leaned on lexical gates — the
31	   SC#6/SC#2 source greps over `crates/fuse`, a vector-"parity" script that
32	   checked files exist and are valid JSON, grep-shaped acceptance criteria
33	   that forced a runtime-broken implementation past review while only a live
34	   suite caught it. v2 gates run code: the KAT manifest, simulation
35	   scenarios, live contract tests. Grep may serve as a hygiene lint; it is
36	   never the proof of an invariant — invariants live in structure and are
37	   exercised by tests.
38	3. **Determinism is injected, not hoped for.** Core takes entropy, time, and
39	   policy as parameters; the engine takes every capability as a seam trait;
40	   the sync timing profile is environment-scoped. Together these move race,
41	   rotation, and offline coverage from flaky wall-clock e2e (v1's only home
42	   for them) into deterministic in-process tests, and make the e2e that
43	   remains fast and sleep-free.
44	
45	What dies relative to v1 — with what killed it:
46	
47	| Gone                                                                                                       | Killed by                                                                                                                 |
48	| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
49	| Lockstep TS/Rust vector suites, `tests/vectors/` twin consumers, `check-vector-parity.sh`                  | #27 D2 — one implementation; the KAT manifest defends the frozen contract; the WASM CI run is the residual parity surface |
50	| `apps/web` unit tests with no CI runner; the `.spec.ts`/`.test.ts` include trap                            | #28 D1 — web keeps no logic worth unit-testing; the merge-blocking browser suite moves to `packages/client`               |
51	| Post-merge-only web/desktop e2e (`ci-e2e.yml` on main push)                                                | the PR e2e gate below — a smoke slice blocks every PR, the full matrix blocks main                                        |
52	| SC#6/SC#2 grep gates standing in for resolve/rotation invariants                                           | engine structure — one gated resolve path exists at all (#33 D7); simulation scenarios exercise it                        |
53	| `check-api-client.sh`, `api:generate` drift job, generated-client compile checks as "contract enforcement" | #28 D6 — the live contract suite against a real API                                                                       |
54	| Mock-heavy Nest specs green while the runtime threw (the take-pagination class)                            | the contract suite runs the real app + Postgres on every PR                                                               |
55	| Serial single-worker e2e whose cascade aborts masked late specs                                            | per-test vault isolation via test-login → parallel workers                                                                |

60	## Suite map
61	
62	### crates/core — KATs and property tests
63	
64	The KAT regime itself is fixed in core.md (manifest, accept+reject vectors,
65	separation KAT, anti-vacuity, committed generators). This doc owns its CI
66	wiring and adds the property layer:
67	
68	- **Manifest job, merge-blocking**: `cargo test` runs the full KAT suite
69	  natively **and** as WASM (the residual parity surface — u64/BigInt,
70	  getrandom wiring). The manifest completeness check — every structure tag,
71	  KDF edge, and codec enumerated has vectors; counts hard-asserted — fails
72	  the job, not a warning. Vectors regenerate only through the committed
73	  generators; a vector diff without a generator diff fails review by
74	  convention and the anti-vacuity counts by construction.
75	- **Property tests** — a new discipline; v1 had zero proptest/fuzzing
76	  anywhere. proptest over: encode∘decode identity including unknown-field
77	  byte-stable round-trip, canonicality rejection (mutated encodings must
78	  reject), the strict name comparator (idempotence, symmetry, platform
79	  agreement), KDF-edge separation over random inputs, IPNS name codec
80	  round-trip. Failing seeds are committed as regression vectors. Case counts
81	  are bounded for CI speed (engineering judgment).
82	
83	### crates/engine — seam fakes and the simulation harness
84	
85	Every seam is a trait, so the engine test kit ships in-memory fakes: a
86	virtual-clock `Scheduler`, an in-memory `RecordTransport` (a fake
87	`/routing/v1` record store), `FloorStore`, `StagingStore`, `Mailbox`, and
88	seeded entropy. No network, no docker, no wall clock — CAS races and
89	multi-day EOL timelines execute in milliseconds.
90	
91	The **simulation harness** is this strategy's center of gravity: N engine
92	instances (owner, write-grantee, read-grantee, revokee, adversary) share one
93	fake record store and mailbox and are stepped deterministically on virtual
94	time. The scenario matrices are mandatory and mirror the design tables 1:1,
95	hard-asserted the same way the KAT manifest is (a table row without a
96	scenario fails the meta-test):
97	
98	- the six adoption-gate stages — acceptance plus every reject class, each
99	  surfacing its named trust-violation error;
100	- the floor law — cold-seed from the re-point object, monotonic advance on
101	  AAD-confirmed unseals, regression rejection, pointer-driven advance;
102	- all five rebase races from the #33 D5 table (conditional delete,
103	  rename/rename, add/add auto-suffix, dest-first move, dual-link repair);
104	- the rotation trigger table and the eager-set law — owner cascade vs
105	  grantee flat, sweep idempotence, concurrent sweepers, resumed name waves
106	  via the history link;
107	- the keyless re-PUT adversary (#38) — forged old-epoch records at old
108	  names, re-point adoption, the pin-window bound;
109	- revocation classification (revocation-signal vs unresolvable vs epoch-lag)
110	  and the withheld-update escalation;
111	- the offline queue — FIFO replay through rebase, dead-letter on
112	  revoked-while-offline with staged bytes preserved, staging-budget
113	  fail-fast.
114	
115	Adversarial cases are first-class: the harness can replay, transplant, and
116	re-sign records with any key it holds; every crypto-review finding (#35)
117	gets a pinned regression scenario.
118	
119	### The contract suite — the live API gate
120	
121	The sdk-e2e descendant (#28 D6), and it inherits sdk-e2e's most valuable v1
122	property: it runs on **every PR**. A Rust integration-test crate constructs
123	real engines with production seam implementations pointed at the CI stack
124	(real NestJS app + Postgres + Kubo + the `/routing/v1` store), drives facade
125	commands, and asserts API-side effects. Contract drift between server
126	behavior and the hand-written client fails a test run, not a grep.
127	
128	Coverage, mirroring api.md surface for surface: challenge-signature login,
129	refresh rotation, SIWE secondary; test-login environment gating asserted
130	(production mode must refuse); **register-first fail-closed** — publishing
131	an unregistered name is refused; batch register/retire idempotency; union
132	liveness and refcounted physical unpin; quota (hosted authoritative, BYO
133	`advisory: true`); hosted upload; the mailbox lifecycle (post/poll/ack,
134	idempotency keys, pending-cap reject-new, unknown-recipient rejection);
135	the recovery endpoint (auth + rate limit); account hard-delete cascade;
136	the republisher module's inventory walk and resolve-failure alerting; and
137	**throttling asserted effective** — expect real 429s (v1's inert `@Throttle`
138	decorators are a named defect, api.md). The API's committed OpenAPI artifact
139	gets a freshness check (regenerate-and-diff) as documentation hygiene — it
140	is not the contract gate.
141	
142	### Host suites
143	
144	- **`packages/client` — the merge-blocking browser suite.** The structural
145	  answer to v1's least-verified-layer trap (web-client.md): leadership
146	  election and the single-writer invariant, leader failover with rehydration
147	  from durable seams (kill the leader, assert no accepted-op loss), both
148	  facade transports, and the Service Worker brokerage — in a real browser
149	  against real IndexedDB, OPFS, Web Locks, and BroadcastChannel, driven by
150	  Playwright. This suite blocks every PR.
151	- **Seam conformance kits.** The engine ships a reusable conformance suite
152	  per seam trait — FloorStore monotonicity and durability semantics,
153	  StagingStore ordering and orphan GC, SnapshotCache ciphertext-only-at-rest
154	  — that every real implementation must pass: browser implementations inside
155	  the browser suite, desktop implementations in cargo tests. One contract,
156	  every platform; the v1 per-platform store-drift class has no home.
157	- **`crates/fuse` operation core.** vfs operations driven directly against a
158	  real engine on fake seams — no kernel, runs on any CI runner. Covers the
159	  never-block law (no operation may await network), name validation and
160	  platform-junk filtering, inode stability across renames, and the
161	  errno/status mapping per adapter. The vendored fuser MSG_PEEK patch gets
162	  the regression test desktop.md commits to. Windows CI compiles and tests
163	  the thin WinFsp adapter and remains authoritative for it — but the
164	  operation core no longer lives there.
165	- **`apps/api` unit.** Nest specs where server logic actually lives (quota
166	  arithmetic, refcounting, retention caps, auth services) — the v1 jest
167	  setup ports. The contract suite, not spec mocks, is the correctness gate.
168	- **`apps/web` and `apps/desktop` shells.** No unit suites, by design — v1's
169	  accidental posture made policy (and made safe: the logic genuinely lives
170	  below the facade now). Playwright and the mounted e2e cover rendering and
171	  chrome.
172	
173	### E2E — flows over real stacks
174	
175	- **Web Playwright** ports the v1 skeleton from `tests/web-e2e/`: the
176	  page-object model, fixtures, the wallet-mock SIWE login, multi-account
177	  helpers, and test-login API helpers — rewired to v2. The DEV-gated facade
178	  introspection hook (snapshot and event-stream taps, no key access)
179	  replaces v1's window-store poking as the e2e seam; deterministic waits
180	  poll it — never sleep. Tests run against the production build served
181	  statically (v1 tested the Vite dev server; the artifact that ships was
182	  never the artifact tested). Per-test vault isolation via test-login makes
183	  workers parallel; `retries: 0` ports as policy — a flaky test is a defect.
184	- **Desktop mounted e2e** keeps the v1 shape that worked: dev-key headless
185	  entry, real mounts per platform (FUSE-T SMB, libfuse3, WinFsp), the
186	  orchestrator scripts and wait-for-mount pattern — scenarios rewritten onto
187	  the new facade: mount round-trip, conflict outcomes, cross-client sync,
188	  and the new offline-replay and rotation-under-mount flows (desktop.md).
189	- **Cross-client e2e** — the marquee v2 addition: web and desktop hosts (or
190	  two instances of one host) on a single vault, exercising share
191	  grant/accept, the revocation immediate cut, write rotation with surviving
192	  grantees, offline/reconnect convergence, and leader failover mid-flow
193	  (web-client.md). Runnable at all only because of the DX hook below.

195	## CI gates
196	
197	Path-filtered like v1 (the dorny pattern and reusable-workflow structure
198	port), reorganized into three tiers:
199	
200	| Tier                         | Trigger        | Contents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
201	| ---------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
202	| **PR gate** — merge-blocking | every PR       | lint + typecheck; cargo workspace tests (core KATs + property layer, engine simulation, fuse op core); the WASM KAT run; the `packages/client` browser suite; the contract suite on the CI stack; Windows cargo check + adapter tests; DB migration drift check (ports as-is if the API keeps TypeORM); an e2e **smoke slice** — a bounded-minutes budget of web login-and-CRUD plus one timing-profile cross-client scenario |
203	| **Main gate**                | push to main   | the full web-e2e suite, the desktop mounted matrix (macOS/Linux/Windows), the full cross-client matrix. Failure is treated revert-first, not fix-forward — this tier exists to bound the blast radius of what the smoke slice missed, never to be the first line                                                                                                                                                              |
204	| **Dispatch / scheduled**     | manual or cron | the load harness (v1's k6 scenarios in `tests/load/` port); long-horizon liveness — lease renewal at seq+1 and the republisher walk against a compressed-EOL profile; staging release gates (mechanics → [#48](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/issues/48))                                                                                                                                                            |
205	
206	The CI stack: Postgres, Kubo, the API under test, and a local `/routing/v1`
207	record store — v1's `mock-ipns-routing` tool **promoted, not deleted**: a
208	dumb delegated-routing server is exactly the RecordTransport seam's shape,
209	so the hermetic CI store and production someguy are interchangeable behind
210	the same client code. someguy itself runs in staging, not CI (the real DHT
211	has no place in a hermetic gate). The v1 redis/tee-worker services leave the
212	stack; the local/CI redis port split (6380/6379) dies with them.

214	## The DX hook — the environment-scoped timing profile
215	
216	The sync timing profile (#33 D3) is the single lever that makes v2's
217	cross-client flows testable at speed, and this doc is its consumer contract:
218	
219	- **CI profile**: record TTL 1–5 s (small but nonzero — `0`/unset is how v1
220	  fell into a silent 5-minute default), compressed poll cadence, staleness
221	  thresholds, escalation window, pointer-consult interval, and a small
222	  staging budget so budget-exhaustion paths are reachable. Production
223	  profile: TTL 1 minute, 30 s poll, per #33.
224	- **Nocache manual refresh** is the TTL-independent forcing path — the
225	  deterministic sync barrier between clients in every cross-client scenario.
226	- **No sleeps anywhere**: web polls the introspection hook, desktop polls
227	  the filesystem and tray state, both bounded by profile-derived timeouts.
228	- **The profile is where measured constants land.** The open-edge numbers
229	  the sibling docs handed here — the migration-window closure constant, the
230	  sweep cadence, kernel entry/attr TTLs per backend, chunk size and DAG
231	  shape — get their values from measurements this harness produces (the
232	  cross-client latency measurement job, the FUSE-T invalidation round-trip,
233	  ranged-fetch profiles). Each lands as a profile-constant change with its
234	  measurement linked. The process is fixed here; the values are build-time
235	  work.
236	
237	## Hardware verification gates
238	
239	The #32 pre-build checks, owned here as task-shaped verifications with
240	recorded results — they precede `crates/fuse` work, and they are not CI:
241	
242	1. FUSE-T ≥ 1.2.7 SMB invalidation round-trip, with measured cross-client
243	   latency — feeds the kernel TTL constants above.
244	2. Replay of the v1 macOS cross-client flake scenario against the SMB
245	   backend.
246	3. Overwrite-rename atomicity under the SMB backend.
247	4. FUSE-T commercial license terms for bundling.
248	5. The FSKit spike against the macOS 27 beta
249	   (`mountSingleVolume`/`DataCacheHandler` behavior).
250	
251	Results are recorded alongside the profile constants they feed; a failed
252	gate reopens the driver decision (#32), not this doc.
253	
254	## Coverage policy
255	
256	No blanket line-coverage thresholds as merge gates. v1's record: the
257	sdk-core 80% gate broke on barrel-file refactors while real gaps hid
258	elsewhere; api-client ran a 0% threshold with `passWithNoTests` — pure
259	theater. Codecov stays as informational reporting. The merge gates are
260	structural instead: KAT-manifest completeness, the simulation harness's
261	table-mirroring anti-vacuity assertions, seam conformance kits, and the
262	named CI jobs above — each asserts _presence of specific coverage_, which a
263	percentage never did.
264	
265	## Disposition of the v1 inventory
266	
267	| v1 artifact                                                                                             | Disposition                                                                                         |
268	| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
269	| `tests/web-e2e/` (Playwright skeleton, wallet-mock, page objects, test-login helpers)                   | **Ports** — rewired to the facade introspection hook and built-artifact serving                     |
270	| `POST /auth/test-login` (prod hard-block, `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` timing-safe check, deterministic keypair) | **Ports** — same gating pattern; v2 derivation feeds `start(secret)`                                |
271	| `tests/sdk-e2e/`                                                                                        | **Succeeded** by the contract suite — keeps its PR-blocking slot and stack recipe                   |
272	| `tests/desktop-e2e/` (run-all orchestrators, wait-for-mount, dev-key mode, `.mts`/tsx invocation)       | **Ports** — scenarios rewritten onto the facade                                                     |
273	| `docker/docker-compose.yml` postgres/kubo services; GH service-container pattern                        | **Ports**                                                                                           |
274	| `tools/mock-ipns-routing`                                                                               | **Promoted** — the hermetic `/routing/v1` CI record store                                           |
275	| someguy service                                                                                         | staging/production accelerator only — leaves CI                                                     |
276	| redis, tee-worker services and their secret plumbing                                                    | **Die** (#24)                                                                                       |
277	| `ci.yml` job skeleton, dorny path filters, reusable workflows, failure-artifact uploads                 | **Port** — refiltered for the v2 layout                                                             |

288	  engineering judgment at build time, revisited as the suite grows.

291	- **Web3Auth Core Kit interactive login** — wallet-mock covers SIWE in CI;

You are implementing GitHub issue #624 for the CipherBox v2 rewrite, working in an isolated git worktree of /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box (branch off `main`).

## Issue #624 — "api: build identity auth, refresh rotation, and the ops baseline"

Scope (verbatim):
users/auth_methods/refresh_tokens migrations; challenge-signature login against the secp256k1 identity key; SIWE as secondary auth; short-lived access JWT + rotating refresh token; implicit account creation at first login; staging-gated test-login; a working global throttler with per-surface limits (v1's inert @Throttle is a named defect); Prometheus metrics on the health stub; OpenAPI document emitted from decorators and committed as a docs artifact.
Does NOT land: deletion cascade, quota, any pin/name surface.

Gate: New named api-unit job + migration-drift job (TypeORM drift check returns) + openapi-freshness diff job, all merge-blocking day one (added to .github/workflows/ci.yml on the PR trigger). Contract-suite coverage arrives with a later slice — do not build it.

## Required reading BEFORE writing code

1. `blueprint/api.md` in the repo — sections: Identity and auth; Account lifecycle (creation); Ops; Contract and clients. This is NORMATIVE. Follow it exactly.
2. `CONTEXT.md` — the ubiquitous language; use its terms exactly.
3. `AGENTS.md` — project rules (security rules, naming conventions, commit format).
4. `blueprint/testing.md` — laws: every suite must block a merge in a named CI job the day it lands; assert behavior, never source text.

## Current state

- `apps/api` is a fresh minimal NestJS 11 scaffold (main.ts, app.module.ts, health controller, vitest for tests). Build it out from here.
- v1's full API is frozen on branch `v1` (tag `v1-freeze`). You may consult it read-only via `git show v1:apps/api/...` / `git ls-tree -r v1 --name-only -- apps/api` for porting patterns (e.g. the v1 `POST /auth/test-login` prod hard-block + TEST_LOGIN_SECRET timing-safe check pattern, challenge-signature login, TypeORM migration-drift check script/workflow). Port patterns, but conform to blueprint/api.md where it differs from v1. NEVER modify branch v1.
- Postgres: docker/docker-compose.yml has a postgres service. You may start it (`docker compose up -d postgres` from docker/) for migration validation. Do NOT `docker compose down` shared infra when done — leave the stack running.

## Hard rules

- Work only in: `apps/api/**`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (add the three named jobs), root config only if strictly required (e.g. pnpm-workspace already includes apps/*). Do NOT touch `crates/**` (another agent is working there), `blueprint/**`, `docs/**`, branch v1, or unrelated files.
- First: run `pnpm install` in the worktree (never symlink node_modules from the main checkout).
- Create a feature branch: `feat/api-identity-auth-ops-baseline` (the worktree may already be on a generated branch — rename/create as needed).
- Commits: Conventional Commits, e.g. `feat(api): ...`. NO parentheses in the subject line after the type/scope — a custom commitlint rule rejects parenthesized text in the subject. Commit your work incrementally to the feature branch. Do NOT push. Do NOT create a PR.
- TypeScript: prefer string literals over TS enums. camelCase for API fields, snake_case for DB columns. Never log or store sensitive keys.
- Zero-knowledge server: the server never sees plaintext or unencrypted keys. Auth verifies signatures over server-issued challenges; it never receives private keys.
- If you write/modify `.md` files: markdownlint runs on commit — no `**bold**` as headings (use `###`), blank lines around code fences and lists.

## The codec API you are testing (already on disk — read these files first)

- `crates/core/src/codec/mod.rs` — exports `encode(&Value) -> Vec<u8>`, `decode(&[u8]) -> Result<Value, CodecError>`, `decode_map_partial(bytes, is_known) -> Result<(Map, UnknownFields), CodecError>`, `encode_map_partial(&Map, &UnknownFields) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError>`, `known_key_set`, `Value`, `Map`, `canonical_key_cmp`, `MAX_DEPTH = 128`.

- `Value::Display` renders CBOR diagnostic notation (see value.rs `write_diag_text` for escaping rules); accept vectors pin it via a `diag` field.
- Depth semantics: top-level item is read at depth 0; each container level +1; an item at depth >= 128 rejects `depth-exceeded`. So 128 nested arrays accept; 129 reject.

1. `crates/core/kat/manifest.json` — the machine-checked manifest. camelCase JSON fields. Shape:

     "profile": "cipherbox/v2 det-cbor",
     "codecs": {
       "det-cbor": {
         "accept": { "file": "vectors/codec/accept.json", "count": <exact>, "requiredKinds": [...] },
         "reject": { "file": "vectors/codec/reject.json", "count": <exact>, "checks": [<the 15 decode-reachable check names>] },
         "unknownFields": { "file": "vectors/codec/unknown_fields.json", "count": <exact> }
       }
     },
     "structureTags": {},
     "kdfEdges": {}
   }
   structureTags/kdfEdges are deliberately present-and-empty: the spine later slices extend. The 15 decode-reachable checks = all 5 trust checks + all malformed checks EXCEPT unexpected-type and unknown-field-collision (those two are encode-side/schema-side, pinned by unit tests in src/codec/fields.rs).

2. `crates/core/kat/vectors/codec/accept.json` — array of `{ "name", "hex", "diag", "kinds": [...] }`. Lowercase hex. Required coverage (this drives requiredKinds; use these kind tags): uint boundaries 0, 23, 24, 255, 256, 65535, 65536, 4294967295, 4294967296, u64::MAX; negint -1, -24, -25, and -2^64 (Value::Negative(u64::MAX), diag "-18446744073709551616"); bytes empty/short/a 24+-length one (length-header class change); text empty/ascii/multibyte-unicode/24+-length; array empty/nested/heterogeneous; map empty/multi-key exercising canonical sort order (keys of different lengths, e.g. "a","b","aa" — shorter sorts first)/nested; bool true/false; null; a 128-deep nested-array vector at the depth limit. ~30+ vectors.

3. `crates/core/kat/vectors/codec/reject.json` — array of `{ "name", "hex", "check", "class" }`. At least one vector per decode-reachable check, several for the load-bearing ones. Must include these specific regression pins:
   - `f90014` → float-forbidden (half-float whose bit pattern aliases simple value 20/false — a real bug class in this decoder's history)
   - `f814` → simple-value-forbidden (two-byte form of simple 20 must NOT alias false)
   - `d82a4500010203aa`-style tag-42 vector → tag-forbidden (DAG-CBOR CID links are outside this profile) — any well-formed tag-42 item is fine
   - non-canonical-uint: 1817 (23 in 8-bit form), 1900ff, 1a0000ffff, 1b00000000ffffffff, and a negative-int variant 3817
   - non-canonical-length: an 8-bit length form for a <24-length string (e.g. 5803 + 3 bytes), plus array/map variants (9803.../b801...)
   - indefinite-length: 5f/7f/9f/bf openers (e.g. 5f41aaff)
   - unsorted-map-keys: bytewise violation {"b":1,"a":2} AND a length-order violation {"aa":1,"b":2} (canonical order is length-first for text keys)
   - duplicate-map-key: a2616101616102
   - truncated: bare 18; a bytes head claiming more than present; an array missing an element; empty input ("")
   - trailing-bytes: 0100
   - invalid-utf8: 62fffe
   - invalid-map-key-type: a10102 (int key)
   - reserved-additional-info: 1c, and 1f (major 0 ai 31)
   - unexpected-break: ff
   - depth-exceeded: 129 nested arrays (generator-computed)
   Verify every hex you write actually produces that check by running it through the decoder (write the generator first, have it assert; do not hand-guess byte meanings).

4. `crates/core/kat/vectors/codec/unknown_fields.json` — array of `{ "name", "hex", "knownKeys": [...], "expectUnknownCount": n }`. Test contract: decode_map_partial(hex, key in knownKeys) succeeds, unknown.len() == expectUnknownCount, encode_map_partial(known, unknown) == hex (byte-stable). Cases: all-known, none-known, interleaved known/unknown in canonical order, an unknown value that is itself a nested map/array, empty map. ~6+ vectors.

5. `crates/core/examples/kat_gen.rs` — THE committed generator (blueprint: vectors regenerate only through committed generators, never hand-edits). Run as `cargo run -p cipherbox-core --example kat_gen`. It: builds accept + unknown-field vectors from Value constructors + `encode`; holds reject vectors as explicit commented byte literals (hand-crafted bytes are the point for reject vectors — do not derive them from the encoder); ASSERTS every vector against the live codec (accept: decode+re-encode+diag; reject: check+class; unknown: round-trip) so a generator run is itself a self-check; writes the three JSON files (serde_json pretty, trailing newline) and rewrites manifest.json counts/checks/requiredKinds in place from the generated data (preserving manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges). Use CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR-relative paths so it runs from any cwd. Generate the actual files by running it.

6. `crates/core/tests/kat_manifest.rs` — the manifest job (merge-blocking; must also run under wasm32-wasip1, so load fixtures with include_str!, never fs at runtime). Structure: serde structs with #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] for manifest + vector files. Assertions (each a named #[test]):

   - counts exact: manifest count == vector array length, per file
   - names unique within each vector file
   - reject checks: manifest checks list == exactly the distinct checks appearing in reject vectors; every entry ⊆ TrustViolation::CHECKS ∪ Malformed::CHECKS; ALL 5 TrustViolation::CHECKS present; the only CHECKS absent are exactly {"unexpected-type", "unknown-field-collision"} (hardcode that exclusion with a comment saying they're unit-test-pinned in src/codec/fields.rs)

   - run all accept vectors: decode succeeds, re-encode == input bytes, format!("{value}") == diag
   - run all reject vectors: decode fails, err.check() == check, err.class() == class
   - run all unknown-field vectors per the contract above

You are implementing GitHub issue #623 for the CipherBox v2 rewrite, working in an isolated git worktree of /Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box (branched from `main`).

## Issue #623 — "engine: scaffold seams, fakes, conformance kits, and the facade"

Scope (verbatim):
The nine seam traits (FloorStore, RecordTransport, Http, Mailbox, RefreshHintSource, Scheduler, StagingStore, SnapshotCache, CredentialStore) as opaque-byte/event contracts; the constructor takes the seam set whole (missing seam = compile error). The engine test kit's in-memory fakes (virtual-clock Scheduler, fake /routing/v1 record store, in-memory stores, seeded entropy); the reusable per-seam conformance kits, proven by the fakes passing them; the sync timing profile type with production and CI profiles; the facade skeleton — the single async command-and-event surface with start of secret.
Does NOT land: pipeline logic, real seam implementations (those live in hosts and pass the kits there).

Gate: New merge-blocking engine job inside the PR-gate cargo workspace tests: engine unit tests + every seam conformance kit executed against its in-memory fake. Add it as a named job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (PR trigger), following the existing job style (pinned action SHAs, dorny path-filter gating on the `rust` output, cargo cache pattern — copy from the cargo-linux job).

## Required reading BEFORE writing code (all in the repo)

1. `blueprint/engine.md` — IN FULL. It is normative, especially: Doctrine; Module map; Host seams (the exact seam trait contracts and their semantics); Facade. Follow its naming and shape exactly — this scaffold defines the architecture every downstream engine/web/desktop slice builds on.
2. `CONTEXT.md` — ubiquitous language; use its terms exactly (sync timing profile, adoption gate, floor law, op queue, …).
3. `AGENTS.md` — project rules.
4. `blueprint/testing.md` — the seam-fake/conformance-kit strategy ("crates/engine — seam fakes and the simulation harness", "Seam conformance kits") and law 1 (named merge-blocking CI job same PR).

## Current state

- `crates/engine` is a stub (lib.rs with a placeholder CRATE const and a `depends_on_core` test referencing `cipherbox_core::CRATE`). Note: another in-flight PR (#618) replaces `cipherbox_core::CRATE` with real codec modules — do not rely on core beyond what main has today; if you need nothing from core yet, keep the dependency but drop usages that would conflict (you may rewrite the placeholder tests entirely; a trivial rebase conflict with #618 in lib.rs is expected and fine).
- Workspace: Cargo workspace at repo root, edition 2024, rust-version 1.88, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` convention, clippy -D warnings and cargo fmt enforced in CI.

## Design constraints

- Determinism is injected: entropy, time, and policy enter as parameters/seam traits — no direct clock or RNG calls anywhere in engine logic. The virtual-clock Scheduler fake and seeded entropy are the test kit's levers.
- Seam traits are opaque-byte/event contracts: `Vec<u8>`/`&[u8]` payloads, no domain types leaking into seams (the engine owns interpretation).
- The engine constructor takes the full seam set as one struct/type-checked bundle — a missing seam is a compile error, not a runtime panic.
- Conformance kits: reusable test suites, one per seam trait with durable semantics (at minimum FloorStore monotonicity/durability, StagingStore ordering/orphan-GC, SnapshotCache ciphertext-only-at-rest semantics — follow blueprint/engine.md's contracts), exported so host crates can run them against real implementations later (e.g. a `pub fn conformance` module compiled under a feature like `test-kit` or in a `testkit` module — choose the shape blueprint/engine.md implies and justify it in your report).
- Sync timing profile: an environment-scoped struct with explicit production and CI constants per blueprint/testing.md "The DX hook" (record TTL, poll cadence, staleness thresholds, escalation window, pointer-consult interval, staging budget). TTL always explicit — no zero/unset default.
- Facade skeleton: the single async command-and-event surface with `start(secret)` — skeleton only, commands may return unimplemented-style typed errors, but the surface shape (command enum/methods + event stream) must be real. No pipeline logic.
- Async runtime choice must respect that the engine compiles both natively and (later) to WASM in a worker — avoid tokio-specific APIs in the public surface; prefer runtime-agnostic futures/channels. Check blueprint/engine.md and blueprint/web-client.md for what they prescribe before picking dependencies; keep the dependency set minimal.

## Hard rules

- Work only in: `crates/engine/**`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (one new named job), root `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` only if adding workspace deps requires it. Do NOT touch `crates/core` source, `apps/**`, `blueprint/**`.
- Branch: create `feat/engine-seams-fakes-facade-scaffold` in your worktree. Conventional Commits; NO parentheses in the commit subject line. Commit incrementally. Do NOT push. Do NOT create a PR.
- Quality bar: `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine` green; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml` clean (actionlint is installed).
- Do not run full workspace test suites repeatedly; scope test runs to -p cipherbox-engine (a full `cargo test --workspace` once at the end is fine).

## Report back

Branch, worktree path, commit SHAs, the nine trait signatures you froze (one line each), the conformance-kit export shape you chose and why, dependency additions, test counts, and any deviation from blueprint/engine.md with rationale. Base directory for this skill: /Users/myankelev/.claude/skills/code-review

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** — does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** — does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / PRD / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point — a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here — not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) — fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A PRD/spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below — a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation — and, like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name** — a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code** — the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy** — a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps** — the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession** — a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches** — the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery** — one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change** — one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality** — abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains** — long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man** — a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest** — a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

Send a single message with two `Agent` tool calls. Use the `general-purpose` subagent for both.

**Standards sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full — the sub-agent has no other access to it.
- The brief: "Report — per file/hunk where relevant — (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls — documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings — the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes — that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.
